top_stories.title: Millions of AI agents imperiled by critical vulnerability in open source package
top_stories.summary: A critical security vulnerability has been discovered in a widely used open source package that underpins millions of AI agents. The flaw poses significant risks to AI infrastructure built on the affected software. The story highlights growing security concerns as agentic AI deployments scale rapidly.

top_stories.title: What Pope Leo XIV's First Encyclical Says About the Power of AI
top_stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical addresses the societal and ethical implications of artificial intelligence, marking a significant moment in religious engagement with AI governance. The document reflects on the power dynamics and human consequences of AI development. Anthropic's Christopher Olah was among those invited to the encyclical's presentation at the Vatican.

top_stories.title: Why the Vatican Invited Anthropic to the Pope's AI Encyclical Presentation
top_stories.summary: Anthropic's interpretability researcher Christopher Olah was invited to the Vatican for the presentation of Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on AI, underscoring the Catholic Church's serious engagement with AI safety research. The invitation reflects the Church's effort to engage directly with leading AI developers on the ethical implications of the technology. The encyclical is being seen as a major religious statement on the risks and responsibilities of AI.

top_stories.title: Rethinking organizational design in the age of agentic AI
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review examines how the rise of agentic AI is forcing companies to reconsider how they structure teams, workflows, and decision-making. The piece explores how autonomous AI systems are blurring traditional organisational boundaries and creating new management challenges. It draws on research and business case studies to outline emerging models for human-AI collaboration.

top_stories.title: Fake academic journals are publishing AI-generated papers under real professors' names
top_stories.summary: Fraudulent academic journals are being used to publish AI-generated research papers falsely attributed to real academics, raising serious concerns about research integrity and the misuse of generative AI. The phenomenon is undermining trust in scholarly publishing and creating reputational harm for the researchers whose names are being used without consent. The issue highlights the intersection of AI misuse and the vulnerabilities of the academic publishing ecosystem.

further_links.title: The AI bubble isn't like the internet bubble
further_links.summary: Cory Doctorow at Pluralistic argues that the current AI investment bubble differs structurally from the dot-com era in ways that make its eventual correction potentially more damaging.

further_links.title: The Download: puncturing the AI jobs panic
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review examines the latest data on AI's actual impact on employment, pushing back against both alarmist and dismissive narratives about job displacement.

further_links.title: AI Is Taking Over the Most Cursed Job in the World
further_links.summary: Wired reports on how AI systems are increasingly being deployed in debt collection, reshaping one of the most fraught and legally complex areas of consumer-facing business. [Metered]

further_links.title: I'm a Professional Fact-Checker. AI Is Wrong More Often Than You Think
further_links.summary: A professional fact-checker writes for Wired about the frequency and nature of AI errors encountered in practice, offering a ground-level critique of AI reliability for information work. [Metered]

further_links.title: Take This Mandatory AI Workplace Training Right Now—or Else
further_links.summary: Wired investigates the growing wave of mandatory AI training programmes being rolled out by employers, and the mixed reactions from workers being required to upskill under pressure. [Metered]

further_links.title: CIOs are enlisting business users to vibe code their own apps
further_links.summary: Enterprise CIOs are increasingly encouraging non-technical business users to build their own internal applications using AI coding tools, in a trend that raises questions about governance and software quality.

further_links.title: Did the Pope use AI to write about the dangers of AI?
further_links.summary: The Verge investigates whether the papal encyclical on AI may itself have been partially drafted using AI tools, adding an ironic dimension to the Vatican's landmark statement on the technology.

further_links.title: Import AI 458: Reckoning with the future; and a singularity story
further_links.summary: Jack Clark's Import AI newsletter reflects on long-term AI trajectories and includes analysis of a speculative singularity scenario alongside commentary on recent AI developments.

further_links.title: I Spent a Week Recording Myself Doing Chores for Money. Who's the Robot Now?
further_links.summary: Wired explores the growing market for human-generated training data, in which people are paid to record everyday physical tasks to teach robots and AI systems how to navigate the real world. [Metered]

ethan_mollick.title: Choosing to Stay Human
ethan_mollick.summary: Ethan Mollick reflects on what it means to deliberately maintain human agency and identity in a world increasingly shaped by AI. The post explores the tension between the efficiency gains AI offers and the personal and societal value of choosing to do things the slower, more human way. Mollick argues that staying human is itself a meaningful choice, not simply a failure to adapt.
